NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 811 3994 0903, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at LaurenP@RollingHillsEstatesCA.Gov.
  Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for
  their consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 811 3994 0903, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JANUARY 26, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:05 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by Silver Spur Little League players Grant Holdsworth, Vivian Holdsworth
and Dylan Huang along with Board Members Zach Holdsworth and Charles Huang.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF JANUARY 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 63540 THROUGH 63588 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $143,343.36 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 010321 THROUGH
  010621; 63480, 63488, 63492, 63498 AND 63134 (VOID); IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $139,873.09 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $283,216.45 WITH
  PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF DECEMBER 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF DECEMBER 2020
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
JANUARY 26, 2021
   RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 12, 2021 SPECIAL MEETING

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JANUARY 12, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  RESOLUTION NO. 2473 APPROVING THE PROPOSED USE OF 2021-22
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) FUNDS

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF
  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that the City typically
supplements CDBG funds with General Funds and TDA funds to complete the City’s annual
sidewalk repair project, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  WAIVE FURTHER READING AND APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2473
  AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF A CONTRACT WITH THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY  COMMUNITY  DEVELOPMENT  COMMISSION  FOR
  PARTICIPATION IN THE PROGRAM FOR FUNDING OF THE ADA ACCESS
  RAMP AND SIDEWALK IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM AS IDENTIFIED IN THE
  PROGRAM AND CONDITIONS ASSESSMENT REPORT DATED APRIL 2,
  2014 IN THE AMOUNT OF APPROXIMATELY $30,050.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution 2473 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT RATE UPDATE
Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JANUARY 26, 2021
 Assistant City Manager Davis reported on the feedback received by the Equestrian Committee
regarding the Waste Management Rate update, which included discussions of composting,
and general frustration at the manure rate increase, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF added that during the Equestrian Committee meeting, staff was
asked to look more deeply into other options related to composting that might be able to work
around the stormwater requirements. She further explained that Waste Management is
assuming the loss from July – December 2020, but intending to capture the loss for January -
July 2021 back from the City.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA inquired about the use of City funds to backfill some of the
shortfall that Waste Management is experiencing as outlined in the staff report; Assistant City
Manager Davis explained that those impacts would be considered and further discussed with
the Solid Waste Subcommittee and brought back to the Council at a future date.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired about the amount of Waste Management’s revenue loss as a
result of the rate increase deferral. Assistant City Manager Davis explained that approximately
35% was deferred, and that there was approximately $36,000 in revenue loss for the six month
period.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN explained that the Solid Waste Subcommittee is still in
discussions with Waste Management, working to find a mutually beneficial and long term
solution.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

This item was received and filed by the City Council.

B.  AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR JOHN AND LYNN TABER GROVE

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired if the cost of future maintenance was included in the bid.
Assistant City Manager Davis explained that it is not an area currently maintained by the City,
and would be part of the City’s ongoing maintenance going forward.

Assistant City Manager Davis and Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba
discussed the drainage, steepness and erosion concerns for the project, in response to
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN suggested the consideration of semi-permeable concrete for the six-
inch pad outlined in detail number nine.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE ATTACHED PLANS, SPECIFICATIONS AND BID
  DOCUMENTS AND AUTHORIZE THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS DUE MARCH
  3, 2021 FOR THE JOHN AND LYNN TABER GROVE PROJECT, IN FINAL
  FORM AND CONTENT SATISFACTORY TO THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

C.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH FEHR & PEERS – LOCAL EARLY
  ACTION PLANNING (LEAP) GRANTS PROGRAM AWARDED PROJECT

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 26, 2021
 Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN confirmed that this agreement is part of the $65,000 LEAP
grant funds received by the City last year.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA appreciated the inclusion of the terms of service, which will
help future considerations made by the General Plan Advisory Committee.

Discussion ensued regarding the analysis of Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) as it relates to this
project and the City’s General Plan.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH FEHR &
  PEERS, FOR SB 743 IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $59,280, IN FINAL FORM AND CONTENT SATISFACTORY TO THE CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION - FISCAL YEARS 2017-18 & 2018-19 “YEAR ONE”
  STORM DRAIN REHABILITATION PROJECT PERFORMED BY SOUTHWEST
  PIPELINE & TRENCHLESS CORPORATION

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that the work was
completed in a timely manner, but the closing paperwork and final cost analysis was delayed
significantly by Southwest Pipeline.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ inquired if it poses any risk to not have the Silver Spring-
Hawthorne connection completed, in which Community Development & Public Works
Director Wahba stated that the section performed well during recent storms with no
significant risks expected from the delay.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that the project came
in under budget but with the significant delay in being able to close out the project, the
budgeted funds were not carried over from year to year, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM
ZERUNYAN. He further explained that the project did not go over budget, however the
budgeting across fiscal years did not carry over as it should have in order to pay for the final
project.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that better coordination for long range projects is
necessary to track what is paid out and what is owed. She inquired what additional costs will
be needed to complete the final section, was this budgeted for, and would it be possible to
share costs with Rancho Palos Verdes? Community Development & Public Works Director
Wahba responded that the majority of the final section is within RHE, and only a small portion
is in the RPV right-of-way, but that a discussion can be had with RPV to see if they are
willing to contribute.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that the $100,000 in
the FY 2020-21 budget includes funds for the final portion to be completed, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 26, 2021
 Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained that the City lists unpaid contractual
obligations as accrued liabilities within the budget, in response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

Discussion ensued about the City’s budget process regarding how these accrued liabilities are
accounted for and tracked.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) AUTHORIZE STAFF TO MAKE A BUDGET ADJUSTMENT IN ACCOUNT
  NO. 5145-430 (INCREASING THE BUDGET FROM $100,000 TO $340,000),
  TO COVER THE COST OF THE PROJECT; 2) AUTHORIZE STAFF TO MAKE
  A THIRD INSTALLMENT PAYMENT TO SOUTHWEST PIPELINE
  CORPORATION IN THE AMOUNT OF $218,625.96; 3) ACCEPT THE
  PROJECT AS COMPLETE; 4) AUTHORIZE THE CITY CLERK TO FILE THE
  NOTICE OF COMPLETION FORM WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  RECORDER’S OFFICE; AND 5) IF NO CLAIMS ARE FILED WITHIN 35 DAYS
  AFTER RECORDATION, DIRECT STAFF TO RELEASE THE 5%
  CONSTRUCTION RETENTION PAYMENT TO SOUTHWEST PIPELINE
  CORPORATION IN THE AMOUNT OF $19,698.38.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
noting that today marks the one year anniversary of the first COVID-19 case reported in Los
Angeles County. Over the last year, there have been over 1 million cases reported in Los
Angeles County and nearly 16,000 deaths, with a total of 206 cases in Rolling Hills Estates and
5 deaths over the last year. The State and County have been experiencing the expected surge
following the recent holidays, however the number of new cases and hospitalizations have
begun to trend downward. Yesterday, Governor Newsom lifted the regional Stay at Home
Orders, resulting in Los Angeles County issuing a new Health Officer Order allowing outdoor
dining at restaurants to resume, as well as allowing hair salons, barber shops, nail salons etc.
to operate indoors at 25% capacity. The vaccine rollout continues, currently allowing for all
those over 65 years of age as well as front-line and healthcare workers to receive available
vaccines. Currently the biggest challenge is the low supply and high demand for vaccines. The
City will continue to keep the community informed as more information becomes available.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN expressed his frustration on behalf of the community about
unfair availability of the vaccines locally compared to other parts of the County.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF received promising information regarding vaccines from a
representative of Supervisor Janice Hahn’s office during that morning’s South Bay Cities
Council of Governments (SBCCOG)’s Senior Working Group meeting.

12.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

13.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN attended the Sanitation District Board meeting virtually last
week on behalf of the Mayor who has a standing conflict at that time each month.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reported that he attended the Los Angeles County West Vector Control
meeting, and that there have been nearly zero cases of West Nile Virus this past year. He also

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 26, 2021
 reported that the audit report was approved, with the ultimate consensus to go to bid for a new
auditor going forward.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reported that the Clean Power Alliance (CPA) will be meeting next
week.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported on a Neighborhood Leadership Group meeting she
attended last Thursday, where an increasing problem of mail crimes was discussed, as well as
theft within parked cars and increased theft of catalytic converters.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that on Thursday, January 28, 2021, the Lomita
Sheriff’s station will be holding a virtual Coffee with a Cop event at 11:00 a.m.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also announced the upcoming Nature Center Community Meeting
to be held on Tuesday, February 9, 2021 at 5:30 p.m.

14.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  2021 POLICY DEVELOPMENT/STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION -SUGGESTED
  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

There was consensus of the Council to conduct the Policy Development Session meeting in
lieu of the regular City Council meeting on Tuesday, March 9, 2021 beginning at 3:00 pm.

City Manager Grammer suggested adding the consideration of an outdoor smoking ban to the
discussion list.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ suggested adding accrual of liability within contracts to the
Administrative Services Department discussion list.

15.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager (Quarterly Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION.

16.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:53 P.M. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting in honor of City
Attorney Don Davis’ father Lloyd Davis who passed away last week. The meeting was
adjourned to the next City Council meeting to be held on Tuesday, February 9, 2021 at 5:30
p.m. for the purpose of a Special community meeting regarding the George F Canyon Nature
Center.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Steve Zuckerman
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
JANUARY 26, 2021
